description: Tests the ability to search for a specific test suite using the search box.
steps: Verify the presence of the search box using its selector.
Click on the search box to focus.
Type a specific test suite name into the search box.
Press 'Enter' or wait for the results to auto-populate.
Verify that the test suite matching the search query is displayed in the table.
Scroll through the table and confirm that only relevant results are shown.
Clear the search box and validate that the full list of test suites reappears.
expected_results: Test suite matching the search query is displayed.
The table updates dynamically to reflect the search results.
Clearing the search box restores the full list of test suites.
edge_cases: Entering a non-existent test suite name should display no results.
Special characters in the search query should not break the functionality.
Very long search queries should not cause UI or performance issues.
Empty search queries should restore the full list of test suites.
Case-insensitive search should match test suites correctly.
data_requirements: A valid test suite name present in the database.
At least one test suite without a matching name for negative testing.
Test suite names with special characters.
A large dataset of test suites to test performance.
Clear instructions for the expected format of search queries.
dependencies: Search functionality implementation in the backend.
Access to the test suites database.
Proper indexing of test suite names for fast retrieval.
api_interactions: GET request to fetch filtered test suite data based on the search query.
Error handling for API failures during the search.
performance_metrics: Time taken to update the table after entering a search query.
Memory usage while handling large datasets in the search results.
accessibility_requirements: Ensure the search box has appropriate ARIA labels.
Keyboard navigation should allow users to focus and type in the search box.
The search results should be easily readable with screen readers.
